n: LSIL on a Pap smear with koilocytes
wrong: Atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASC-US)

ww.High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesi: HSIL cells are smaller and more immature, with a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio and dense, irregular nuclei. The abundant mature cytoplasm and clear halo seen here point to LSIL instead.
ww.Atypical squamous cells of undetermined: ASC-US is an equivocal call: the nuclei are only slightly enlarged, and the changes are too few or too mild to name a lesion. Obvious koilocytes with large nuclei and clear halos, as here, are LSIL.
ww.Reactive squamous cells with inflammatio: Reactive change from inflammation or repair leaves nuclei round, smooth and evenly stained, sometimes with small nucleoli. It lacks the enlarged, irregular nucleus and sharp perinuclear halo of the koilocyte.
ww.Trichomonas vaginalis infection: Trichomonas can leave a clear halo around a normal-sized nucleus (a pseudokoilocyte) among neutrophils, and pear-shaped flagellates may be seen. Here the nucleus is enlarged and irregular, as in a true koilocyte.

look: Compare the large central cell with its neighbors. The pink and blue-green mature squamous cells have tiny, round, dark nuclei, while the central cell has a nucleus several times larger with coarse chromatin, sitting in a sharp clear halo with a dense rim of cytoplasm. This is a koilocyte, the cytopathic effect of productive HPV infection, and it defines LSIL (CIN 1).
findings: Koilocyte: a large squamous cell with an enlarged, irregular nucleus inside a sharp clear perinuclear halo and a dense rim of cytoplasm, the cytopathic effect of productive HPV infection.
Nuclear enlargement: the koilocyte nucleus is several times larger than the tiny round nuclei of neighboring normal squamous cells, with coarse chromatin and an uneven outline.
Binucleate cell: two nuclei sit side by side inside a cleared zone of cytoplasm, another common koilocytic change in LSIL.

Normal comparison cells: pink superficial and blue-green intermediate squamous cells have abundant flat cytoplasm and one small, round, dark nucleus, which sets the size benchmark for the abnormal cells.

ann.l: Koilocyte: This large squamous cell displays a prominent, sharp perinuclear halo (cleared cytoplasm) and a condensed, dark peripheral rim of cytoplasm. This characteristic cytopathic change is caused by productive HPV infection, defining LSIL.

Nuclear enlargement: The nucleus of the koilocyte is several-fold larger than normal, showing coarse, dark chromatin and an irregular nuclear membrane, reflecting active viral replication and genomic instability.
Binucleate cell: Two enlarged nuclei sit side-by-side within a single cleared cytoplasmic space. Binucleation is another classic cytopathic effect of HPV infection commonly observed in LSIL.

Normal squamous cells: These mature cells (pink superficial and blue-green intermediate) have abundant, flat cytoplasm and tiny, round, condensed nuclei. They serve as an internal size benchmark to highlight the abnormal nuclear enlargement in koilocytes.
